messages:
alyssa_cs: FinEdge escalated — after the 03/16 canary their invoice outputs are truncated and line totals are wrong. Happening on /v1/generate, model=redwood-xl-ctl-v2-canary. Customer sample: 'amounts missing' and 'lines cut off'.

kai_eng: Can you paste a sanitized request/response example and whether they're on hosted/dedicated? Also want headers + model param.

alyssa_cs: Hosted. Minimal repro (sanitized):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-xl-ctl-v2-canary",
  "input": "Generate invoice with line items and totals for order 12345",
  "max_output_tokens": 512
}
```
Response (truncated):
```text
...
Item A - $200
Item B - $150
Total: $
```

sam_oncall: I'm seeing a shift in the model metrics right around 03:02 UTC — token_count per request for redwood-xl-ctl-v2-canary dropped ~40% and average output length shortened. Rolling traffic to canary was 50% at 03:00 per rollout-bot.

rollout-bot: canary 'canary-2026-03-16' scaled to 50% at 2026-03-16T03:00:12Z — variant=redwood-xl-ctl-v2-canary, rollout_id=canary-2026-03-16

kai_eng: Initial theory: a trimming/decoding heuristic intended for chat summarization got enabled for the generate endpoint in this canary. Looks like a default 'trim_tail=true' or stricter stop-seq logic. That would cut numeric tails (totals).

kai_eng: Short-term mitigations:
- Route FinEdge traffic to stable variant: `redwoodctl routing update --customer FinEdge --model redwood-xl-ctl-v2-stable`
- Or set `max_output_tokens` and explicit stop sequence in their request temporarily to avoid premature trimming.

jordan_pdm: We need a customer-facing note. Keep it short: acknowledge, say rollback in progress, ETA ~1h, workaround to set explicit stop and avoid trusting default trimming. Draft below.

maria_support: Draft to FinEdge: "Thanks for reporting — we've identified a regression in a canary model that shortens some generated invoices. We're rolling back the canary for your traffic now and expect a fix within the hour. Temporary workaround: include an explicit stop token and set max_output_tokens to a higher value. We'll notify you once stable is restored." Want me to send?

alyssa_cs: Sent at 03:22 UTC. Customer asked: will this affect billing/data? They want confirmation invoices won't be altered after rollback.

sam_oncall: Starting rollback command now: `redwoodctl rollout revert --id canary-2026-03-16 --to redwood-xl-ctl-v2-stable` — tracking ticket INF-621. I'll watch metrics and confirm once traffic is back to stable.

metrics-bot: metric update: model=redwood-xl-ctl-v2-canary token_count per request dropped -42% at 03:05 UTC; after rollback token_count restored to baseline at 03:45 UTC. latency +8% during rollback window.

kai_eng: Confirmed root cause: prefix/trimming logic was widened to apply to `generate` path in canary; regression slipped through tests. Fix PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/984 — will hotfix to canary and add unit tests to block trimming on structured finance flows.

jordan_pdm: Action items:
- Ops: add routing guard so customers with billing/financial labels are pinned to stable variants during canaries.
- Eng: add prompt-level opt-out flag for trimming (e.g., `x-disable-trim: true`) and surface in docs.
- CS: follow up with FinEdge and offer audit of invoices generated during 03:00-03:45 UTC.

maria_support: FinEdge acknowledged. They've asked for a short timeline and whether historical invoices need manual review. I'll coordinate audit.

sam_oncall: Rollback complete 03:50 UTC, INF-621 updated with notes. Customer confirms invoices look normal after reprocessing a sample. I'll open a postmortem and link to the outreach message.

kai_eng: We'll push the hotfix and run a targeted canary with extra regression tests for financial templates before re-promoting. PR merged to hotfix branch — will coordinate re-rollout window after validation.

maria_support: I'll follow up with FinEdge with the audit offer and ETA for permanent fix.

sam_oncall: Closing the incident thread here but keeping INF-621 open for PM/eng postmortem. Thanks team :thumbsup:
